Over the past year, I have been working to find a better way to write cross-platform apps. The problems I am trying to solve: - Native frameworks only work on a subset of platforms, so a different implementation of the UI needs to be written per target.
- They are updated at the same pace as the platform itself, which forces the developer to split the user base to be able to use new features, or wait a long time for bugs to get fixed.
- They also force developers to use specific high-level languages, so they are not a good fit for apps with high performance requirements, like creative apps or games.
- Cross-platform frameworks that rely on bundling a browser engine solve the problem of code reuse, but they inherit the limitations of HTML/CSS.
- Those that take control over layout and rendering are not efficient and lightweight enough to be used on the web, and require the use of compiled languages. Ideally, we would be able to bundle the UI framework directly with the application. This would allow developers to use new features and fix issues in the UI framework immediately. It would also allow ideas for improvements to compete in a natural way, rather than being decided by a committee. Uniform is my idea for how we can solve these problems. This is the structure: - A layout and rendering engine written in C, compiled to WASM on the web and native code on all other platforms
